title: Location Data Disclosure
description: Child's device (EE2) transmits live GPS coordinates to the backend (P1) at regular intervals. This action causes the threat because the device shares sensitive location data with an external system.
assumptions: The device is capable of transmitting GPS data and the backend is capable of receiving and storing it.

title: Location Data Transmission
description: The data flow (DF1) transmits live GPS coordinates from the device to the backend. This data-centric threat arises because the transmission of location data (meta-data) can be used to link or identify the parties involved.
assumptions: The device and backend are identifiable by the GPS coordinates being transmitted.

title: Location Data Processing
description: The backend (P1) receives and processes the transmitted GPS coordinates. This action causes the threat because the backend stores or processes location data, which may be used for tracking or profiling.
assumptions: The backend is capable of storing and processing the received GPS data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: Process P1 (Mobile App Backend) shares location data with DataStore DS1 (Location History Store). This constitutes a data disclosure as the process transfers personal data (location pings) to a third-party data store, which may be considered a known or unknown third party depending on the store's scope. The minimality principle is key: only strictly required personal data should be disclosed.
assumptions: The backend process is designed to write location pings to the store.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the store is considered a 'known third party' in the context of this specific flow; depends on the store's data retention policies and scope.

title: Data in Transit
description: Location data in transit (DF2) may be used to link or identify the parties involved in the data flow. This could include metadata about the mobile app, the backend process, or the location history store that allows for correlation of data across different systems.
assumptions: The data in transit includes metadata about the parties being used to link or identify them.
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard data-centric threats apply to the flow itself.

title: Data Disclosure
description: DataStore DS1 receives the location data and may process or store it in a way that causes a threat. This could involve storing the data for future use, sharing it with other systems, or retaining it beyond the necessary retention period, which may constitute a data disclosure.
assumptions: The store processes or stores the data in a way that causes a threat.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the store's processing/storage actions constitute a 'threat' under LINDDUN Pro; depends on specific store configuration.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The mobile app (P1) shares personal location data with the backend (P1) for processing, which constitutes a data disclosure as the data is transferred to a known third party (the backend) for processing.

title: Linking
description: The data flow (DF3) transmits location pings to the backend, potentially allowing the backend to link or identify the user via meta-data about the parties being used to link them.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The geofencing engine (P2) receives the location pings and processes them to check zone entry/exit, which involves processing personal data in a way that causes a threat.

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: The Family Account Store (DS2) shares configured zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) with the Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2). If DS2 is not properly secured or if the zone definitions are not encrypted, an unauthorized party could access this data and potentially use it to identify or track individuals.
assumptions: DS2 is accessible to external entities without proper authentication.

title: Data in Transit Identification
description: The zone definitions (home, school, friend's house) are transmitted from DS2 to P2. If the zone definitions contain identifying metadata (e.g., IP addresses, device IDs, or unique identifiers) that can be used to link or identify the parties involved, this data-centric threat arises during transit.
assumptions: Zone definitions include identifying metadata.

title: Unauthorized Processing of Geofencing Data
description: The Geofencing & Alert Engine (P2) receives the zone definitions and processes them to determine if a user is in a configured zone. If P2 stores or uses this data in a way that causes a threat (e.g., storing it in a database that is later accessed by unauthorized parties), a threat arises at the destination.
assumptions: P2 stores or processes the zone definitions in a way that could be exploited.

title: Unauthorized Access to Geofencing Data
description: The Process (P2) shares arrival/departure notification data with the ExternalEntity (EE1) without verifying the recipient's identity or authorization. This allows EE1 to potentially access sensitive location data for unauthorized purposes.
assumptions: No authentication or authorization mechanism is in place between P2 and EE1.

title: Data Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow (DF5) transmits arrival/departure notification data. The threat arises from the potential use of meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., P2 and EE1) to link or identify them, which could be used for tracking or profiling.
assumptions: The data flow does not include explicit metadata about the parties being used for linking.
uncertainty_note: Assuming no explicit metadata is included in the data flow.

title: Unauthorized Processing of Location Data
description: The Destination (EE1) receives the arrival/departure notification data and processes or stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat. This could involve storing location data without consent or using it for purposes other than the intended geofencing.
assumptions: EE1 does not have explicit consent or authorization to process this data.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: Parent (EE1) shares its identity (name, DOB, school) with the Mobile App Backend (P1) to create the child's profile. This is a valid interaction (Process->Process) and the threat arises at the source element where the act of sharing causes the exposure of sensitive personal data.

title: Data Processing/Storage
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) receives the parent's identity data and stores it in a way that causes a threat. This is a valid interaction (Process->Process) and the threat arises at the destination element where the recipient processes or stores the data.

title: Data Disclosure
description: The backend process (P1) shares account, child profile, and geofence zone data with the Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2). This constitutes a data disclosure as the data is transferred across a boundary to a third party (the store).

title: Data Disclosure
description: The Family Account & Permissions Store (DS2) receives the data from the backend process (P1) and stores it. The threat arises at the destination where the recipient processes or stores the data, potentially exposing it to unauthorized access or misuse.

title: Location Data Disclosure
description: Parent (EE1) shares its current location or location history with the Mobile App Backend (P1) without explicit consent or a data-sharing agreement. This act of sharing causes a privacy threat as the parent entity is disclosing sensitive personal information.

title: Location Data Transmission
description: The data flow (DF8) transmits location data (current location or history) between the Parent (EE1) and the Mobile App Backend (P1). The transmission of location data can be used to link or identify the parties involved, constituting a data-centric threat.

title: Location Data Processing
description: The Mobile App Backend (P1) receives and processes the parent's location data. Processing location data for display or mapping purposes can lead to the exposure of the parent's location history or current location, causing a privacy threat.

title: Unauthorized Access to Location History
description: The data store (DS1) shares location history data with the mobile app backend (P1) without explicit user consent or authentication verification. This allows the backend to access sensitive personal location data that the parent user may not intend to share.
assumptions: The system assumes the parent user has granted broad permissions for location history access.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the parent user has explicitly granted broad permissions; this is a high-risk assumption.

title: Data Linking via Metadata
description: The data flow (DF9) transmits location history data in transit. The metadata associated with this data flow (e.g., source IP, user agent, device type) could be used to link or identify the parent user and the mobile app backend, enabling targeted profiling or tracking.
assumptions: The system does not sanitize or obfuscate the metadata associated with the data flow.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the system implements robust metadata sanitization or obfuscation.

title: Unauthorized Data Processing
description: The mobile app backend (P1) receives the location history data and processes it to serve the parent's map/history view. This processing may involve storing, aggregating, or analyzing the data in ways that cause privacy risks, such as creating detailed location profiles or sharing aggregated data with third parties.
assumptions: The system assumes the backend has appropriate security controls in place to protect the data.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if the backend has appropriate security controls; this is a high-risk assumption.

title: Identity Disclosure
description: The parent entity (EE1) shares its identity (e.g., name, contact info, or other identifying attributes) with the mobile app backend (P1) to facilitate the invitation process. This action causes a privacy threat because the recipient (P1) may use this information to link or identify the parent, potentially violating the parent's privacy rights.
assumptions: The parent entity has a modeled identity that can be exposed during the interaction.

title: Data Linking
description: The data flow (DF10) transmits meta-data about the parties involved (e.g., the parent's identity and the mobile app's identity) in transit. This data-centric threat arises because the mobile app backend (P1) may use this meta-data to link the parent to the app, potentially enabling tracking or identification of the parent.
assumptions: The mobile app backend processes or stores meta-data about the parties being used to link or identify them.

title: Unauthorized Processing
description: The destination element (P1) receives the parent's identity and processes or stores it in a way that causes a privacy threat. The mobile app backend may use this data to link the parent to the app, potentially violating the parent's privacy rights.
assumptions: The mobile app backend processes or stores the parent's identity in a way that causes a privacy threat.

title: Unauthorized Access
description: The backend process (P1) grants access to the secondary guardian (EE3), which is an external entity. This interaction is invalid per the mapping table (Process->ExternalEntity is not a valid interaction type), meaning the backend does not have a modeled flow to share data with an external entity. Consequently, the act of sharing data with an external entity is not a valid privacy threat in this context.
assumptions: The backend process (P1) is a valid process, and the secondary guardian (EE3) is an external entity.
uncertainty_note: The mapping table explicitly excludes 'Process->ExternalEntity' as a valid interaction, suggesting this is not a modeled flow and thus not a valid privacy threat scenario.

title: Unauthorized Access
description: The data flow (DF11) transmits live location data from the backend (P1) to the secondary guardian (EE3). This is a data-centric threat where the data itself (live location) is being shared with an external entity. The act of sharing data with an external entity is not a valid interaction, so this is not a valid privacy threat.
assumptions: The data flow (DF11) exists and transmits live location data.
uncertainty_note: The mapping table excludes 'ExternalEntity->ExternalEntity' as a valid interaction, but this is a Process->ExternalEntity interaction, which is also invalid. The threat is not grounded in a valid interaction.

title: Unauthorized Access
description: The secondary guardian (EE3) receives the live location data from the backend (P1). As an external entity, it does not have a modeled flow to process or store this data in a way that causes a threat. The mapping table excludes 'ExternalEntity->ExternalEntity' as a valid interaction, meaning this is not a valid privacy threat.
assumptions: The secondary guardian (EE3) is an external entity.
uncertainty_note: The mapping table explicitly excludes 'ExternalEntity->ExternalEntity' as a valid interaction, suggesting this is not a valid privacy threat scenario.

title: Unauthorized Access to Aggregated Data
description: The process P1 shares aggregated usage and engagement analytics with an external entity (EE4). If the partner lacks appropriate access controls or if the data is not encrypted, an unauthorized party could access this sensitive information.
assumptions: The partner does not have explicit, granular access controls for this specific data set.

title: Data-Linking via Meta-Data
description: The data flow DF12 transmits usage and engagement analytics. If the partner's metadata (e.g., IP address, device ID, or user ID) is exposed or used to link or identify the data recipients, it creates a data-centric threat.
assumptions: The partner's metadata collection or sharing practices are not adequately secured.

title: Unauthorized Processing of Data
description: The destination element (EE4) receives the analytics data. If the partner processes or stores this data in a way that causes a threat (e.g., storing it in a public database, sharing it with third parties, or using it for profiling without consent), a threat arises.
assumptions: The partner's data processing practices are not adequately secured.

title: Attributable Data Evidence
description: The Child (ExternalEntity EE2) sends a manual check-in/SOS message with their current location to the parent (Process P1). This action attributes the data (the message and its associated location data) to the user, creating a non-repudiation risk where the parent cannot deny the message's existence or the user's intent.
assumptions: The message is successfully transmitted and the parent receives it.

title: Data Processing and Storage
description: The parent Process P1 receives the SOS message and stores it. Processing this data for a manual check-in/SOS may involve storing the message in a database or log, which could be a source of privacy threats if the data is accessed or used without proper authorization.
assumptions: The parent processes the message as intended.
